summary: No irrigation is suggested in the forecast window: stored soil water plus forecast rain should cover crop use. Check your soil moisture in the field.

assumptions.kc_source: FAO-56 Table 12 (sub-humid climate); development/late use the stage midpoint of the linear ramp
assumptions.root_depth_rule: FAO's smaller Zr value for scheduling, scaled by stage (0.3 m early) - a simplification
assumptions.et0_method: Hargreaves (FAO-56 Eq. 52) from forecast Tmin/Tmax; rough, can be off by a wide margin
assumptions.effective_rain: 80% of rain counted (my assumption for runoff); rain below 0.2 x ET0 ignored (FAO-56)
assumptions.initial_moisture: readily available water used up (irrigation due)
assumptions.not_included: capillary rise, salinity, runoff modelling, crop stress effects, local Kc adjustments for humidity and wind

notes: ESTIMATE only, not guaranteed agricultural advice. Verify with field soil-moisture checks and local experts.
Water amounts are NET depths reaching the root zone. The volume you must pump or release is larger and depends on your irrigation method and losses.
Only the 5-day forecast window is covered; run it again as new forecasts arrive.
Crop data note: FAO 'Maize, field (grain)'. Kc end is the midpoint of 0.60-0.35.
disclaimer: ESTIMATE based on a simplified FAO-56 water balance and a weather forecast. It is not guaranteed agricultural advice: check soil moisture in your field and consult local experts.
